newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire to reinforce third city against rebels.
newsitem.headline: Zaire to reinforce third city against rebels.

text.p: Zaire's army, its own counter-offensive blunted by repeated rebel thrusts, said on Thursday that it planned to reinforce Kisangani, headquarters for its military operations in the war zone in the east.

A senior defence ministry official announced the reinforcement plan after acknowledging the fall of the key town of Isiro, 340 km (210 miles) to the northeast of Kisangani -- Zaire's third largest city.
"Isiro was taken by the rebels last night, after two days of heavy fighting. The rebels are now reported to be moving west towards Buta," the official told Reuters.
The rebels say Isiro fell on Tuesday.
"We are planning to send more fresh troops into Kisangani over the weekend. The situation necessitates reinforcements," the official added.
Rebel leader Laurent Kabila has said that Kisangani, staging post for the counter-offensive the army launched on January 20 and strategically placed on the mighty Zaire River, is one of his targets.
So too is ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko's jungle palace at Gbadolite -- although this remains hundreds of km (miles) from the battle-front.
Isiro, a hub connecting routes to Uganda, Sudan and the Central African Republic, was a key base for the army and mercenaries.
It is about 800 km (500 miles) east of Gbadolite, Buta is closer but still 450 km (280 miles) away.

The rebels launched the war in October accusing the Zairean authorities of denying them citizenship. Kabila has given Mobutu, who had prostate surgery in Europe in August, until February 21 to begin talks on stepping down.
The United Nations refugee agency (UNHCR) said at least 6,000 people fleeing the civil war were expected to arrive in neighbouring Zambia by barge later on Thursday.
The refugees were travelling to Zambia's northern Mpulungu district across Lake Tanganyika, UNHCR protection officer Ron Mponda told Reuters.
Their arrival would bring to about 8,300 the number of Zaireans who have crossed the border into Zambia since October.
Meanwhile, a Zairean human rights group said a Zairean journalist had been arrested on charges spreading false rumours about the war.
Nepa Bagili Mutita's monthly paper, The Voice of Islam, published last week what it called a list of people wanted by Kabila and the rebels -- they included Mobutu and Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo.
"Nepa was arrested on Tuesday ... at his house ... for propagating false rumours," the Voice of the Voiceless, one of Zaire's leading human rights groups, said in a statement.
The Voice of Islam is little known and little read in Zaire but the offending issue quickly sold out and news vendors ran off photocopies to meet the high demand.
If convicted, Nepa would face up to three years in jail.
